subject.title: fix(agents): prevent opaque shell commands bypassing auto-review

question: Should automatic review remain restricted to PowerShell and shell-wrapper commands whose complete executed behavior is bound to the reviewed payload, with profiles, remoting modes, stdin, mutable scripts, and encoded carriers always escalated to a human?
rationale: This deliberately changes existing automatic-approval behavior at a command-execution security boundary; only the responsible maintainer can confirm the intended compatibility and security posture.

options.title: Adopt the opaque-carrier boundary
options.body: Keep automatic review only for transparent commands and require human approval whenever startup, remoting, encoded, stdin, or mutable-script behavior is outside the reviewed payload.

options.title: Narrow the blocked categories
options.body: Retain automatic review for a specifically documented subset of currently blocked carriers, with contract evidence and regression coverage for that exception.

recommendation.title: Adopt the opaque-carrier boundary
recommendation.body: Keep automatic review only for transparent commands and require human approval whenever startup, remoting, encoded, stdin, or mutable-script behavior is outside the reviewed payload.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merged and follow-up work directly owns the current shell auto-review policy trail.
